evidence.title: Cosmos Software Factory Agent - Ticket to Code

evidence.title: PR to Merge
evidence.locator: How it works; Where you participate
evidence.finding: Experts review and repair changes. A human decides and performs the final merge. Configured agent approval is separate from merging.

evidence.title: PR Author
evidence.finding: PR Author creates a branch, implements the change, opens a PR or MR and handles CI, merge conflicts and review comments.

evidence.title: Cosmos Week 38 Release Notes

evidence.title: Harness acquires Augment Code to advance the Autonomous SDLC
evidence.locator: Connecting code context; From a downstream finding; Bringing governance

evidence.title: Using Sessions
evidence.locator: About sessions; Session lifecycle; Share a session
evidence.finding: Cosmos supports phone browsers, explicitly has no separate iOS/Android app, saves conversations indefinitely, and gives individually shared users viewer access. Environments pause and may restart clean.

evidence.title: Using Tasklist
evidence.locator: Creating a New Task; Subtasks; Status; Reviewing Changes
evidence.finding: IDE Tasklist supports human and agent creation, editable nested tasks, explicit execution, state indicators, moving lists to a new chat and per-task diff review.

evidence.title: Project Builder
evidence.finding: The Expert drafts a design, iterates with the human, breaks work into tickets and launches PR Author workers in dependency waves. It never writes implementation code or merges.

evidence.title: Auggie Subagents
evidence.finding: Built-in and custom subagents have independent context, tools and prompts, run concurrently and report progress in the parent thread. Configuration includes model and thinking level.

evidence.title: Daemon Workspaces and Isolation
evidence.finding: Isolated daemon sessions get one Git worktree per repository. Shared sessions edit the daemon checkout and may overwrite each other. Isolation requires Git 2.31+.

evidence.title: Install Auggie CLI
evidence.finding: Auggie runs locally or on a server with Node 20+, macOS, Linux or Windows WSL and zsh/bash/fish. Version 1 is prerelease; stable 0.x remains available.

evidence.title: PR Author
evidence.finding: PR Author creates branches and pull or merge requests, follows CI, handles merge conflicts and responds to review comments.

evidence.title: Using Teams
evidence.finding: Administrator manages invites, members, seats, plan and billing. Member can view team information or leave, but cannot administer billing or membership.

evidence.title: Augment Code Pricing
evidence.locator: Plan cards; Usage FAQ; Support FAQ
evidence.finding: Standard is $20/month for up to 50 seats with $20 shared usage; Business is $100. LLM list rates plus 40% service fee, compute without that fee, pooled top-ups valid twelve months. Trials exclude SLA.

evidence.title: Available Models
evidence.finding: Augment lists Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Zhipu, xAI and Moonshot models, subject to organization configuration; model options do not prove external harness support.

evidence.title: Augment Code introduction.md
evidence.locator: Cosmos, Auggie CLI, IDE clients; linked current model/subagent documentation
evidence.finding: The introduction distinguishes the Cosmos automation product, Auggie CLI and Augment IDE clients. The coding workflow is supplied by Augment/Auggie and Cosmos experts; selected Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/xAI model providers do not run those vendors coding CLI harnesses.

evidence.title: Augment Code professional terms of service
evidence.finding: The main software-engineering AI platform is covered by Augment professional terms. Customer access is non-exclusive/non-transferable and limited to internal business use; distribution, reverse engineering and derivative versions are restricted, and the company retains platform intellectual property.

evidence.title: Augment Code pricing
evidence.locator: Public plan cards; Usage, top-up and trial FAQ
evidence.finding: The complete current public plans are paid Standard $20/month, Business $100/month and custom Enterprise. Standard/Business pool model/context/compute dollar usage; top-ups are usage based. Trials have separate support terms, with no recurring free tier listed. No BYOK or one-time purchase plan is listed.

evidence.title: Using Slack as a Tool or Trigger
evidence.locator: Prerequisites; Enabling Slack as a Tool; Configuring Slack Triggers; Workflow and Push Slack Notifications; Known Limitations; Disabling Slack Access
evidence.finding: A tenant admin connects the Slack app; Experts get a tenant-scoped slack-api tool and app_mention/message triggers with JSONLogic filters. @Augment can answer questions, open PRs and run scheduled workflows; workflows post results to Slack channels. Slack-created agents are owned by the bot user.

evidence.title: Using Sessions
evidence.locator: About sessions; Start a session; Write and send a prompt; Attach files; Open a desktop; Session lifecycle; Share a session
evidence.finding: Sessions pair an Expert (instructions, model, capabilities) with an Environment. Cosmos runs in any browser including phones; there is no iOS or Android app. Messages typed while the agent works queue for the next turn. Conversations are saved indefinitely; the Environment pauses when idle, runs up to 24 hours at a time and restarts automatically on the next message. Sessions are Shared or Private; owners grant viewer access.

evidence.title: Introducing Auggie CLI
evidence.locator: Version banner; Getting started; Using Auggie in your automations
evidence.finding: Auggie 1.x is a prerelease on the npm prerelease tag; Node 20+, auggie auth login, project indexed automatically; --print and --mode stream/json for automation. Non-interactive mode may be disabled by enterprise agreement.

evidence.title: Available Models
evidence.locator: Current models; Choosing a model; Notes
evidence.finding: Lists Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Zhipu and Moonshot models (some hosted on Fireworks, Baseten or Vertex AI) plus Prism ensembles; availability is subject to organization model settings. Eligible OpenAI GPT models and Prism can be used without approving provider data retention in org model settings; other models need that approval. Retirement dates are listed.

evidence.title: Token-Based Pricing
evidence.locator: Overview; The Business plan; Per-model rates
evidence.finding: Each request bills LLM tokens at provider public list price, a flat 40% service fee on LLM usage, and Cosmos compute at $0.19/hour in 5-minute increments. Business plan $100/month with $100 included usage, up to 50 seats with no per-seat charge, then pay-as-you-go top-ups at the same rates. USD per-million-token rates per model.

evidence.title: Usage Dashboards & Budgets
evidence.locator: Enterprise note; Organization Usage; My Usage; Budgets; Known Limitations
evidence.finding: Enterprise only. Organization Usage shows per-user and per-model usage with CSV export; My Usage shows model and daily breakdowns. Org, default user and per-user monthly budgets can be enforced (access paused until next month) or tracking-only, with alert thresholds to admins or users. Dashboard refreshes about every 90 minutes; Context Engine MCP usage is not shown.

evidence.title: Configuring Cosmos
evidence.locator: Quickstart; Connect GitHub/Slack/Linear; Understanding your options; Choose a Starting Environment; Add Repositories; Pick Your Experts
evidence.finding: Onboarding connects the Augment GitHub App (admin picks repos), optional Slack and Linear. Self-hosted is one command on a laptop, VM or server; Cloud hosts the VM from a base image (Ubuntu 24.04 default, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Ruby, Rust images) or your own. Cosmos starts the VM, clones repos and creates a snapshot automatically, then you pick Experts and start a session.

evidence.title: Self-Hosted Daemon Overview
evidence.finding: Install Auggie daemon release with npm, log in and run auggie daemon from the workspace; pools group hosts. Messages sent while a daemon is disconnected queue until it reconnects, and the session expects the same filesystem state. Daemons need outbound access to Augment services for inference.

evidence.title: Self-hosted Kubernetes
evidence.finding: Connect a self-hosted Linux-only Kubernetes cluster to Cosmos with Minikube, generated manifests or a Helm chart; requires access to cosmos.augmentcode.com and outbound access to the US or EU Cosmos gateway.

evidence.title: Augment docs index
evidence.finding: Index lists connector guides for Azure DevOps Cloud, GitHub, GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab Cloud and self-hosted, Jira Cloud, ClickUp, Datadog, Linear, Microsoft Teams, Slack and Twingate, and a Cosmos ROI Analyst Expert that reports impact from GitHub PR / GitLab MR activity.

evidence.title: Ticket Manager: from ticket to PR
evidence.locator: From ticket to PR; Connect your tools; Try it in your ticket tracker
evidence.finding: Ticket Manager checks a delegated GitHub Issues, Linear or Jira ticket, asks PR Author to implement it, keeps the ticket updated and links the PR or MR back; humans review and merge. Code hosts: GitHub, GitLab Cloud, Azure DevOps Services, Bitbucket via custom setup. GitHub/Jira delegate by label (removed after the issue is claimed); Linear by delegating to the Cosmos agent.

evidence.title: Managing Cosmos with auggie cloud
evidence.locator: About auggie cloud; API first; Declarative bundles; GitOps workflows
evidence.finding: auggie cloud manages Experts, environments, sessions, triggers, secrets, MCP servers and Spaces through the same control-plane API the web UI uses; most list/get commands accept --json. Experts, environments, MCP servers and residents are YAML bundles with init/export/validate/diff/apply; each apply creates an immutable version. Examples: session create, trigger disable, usage. Service-account tokens authenticate CI.

evidence.title: Analytics API
evidence.finding: Enterprise-only Analytics API in preview with v0 endpoints for DAU counts, daily usage and user activity.

evidence.title: Using Auggie with Automation
evidence.finding: Session tokens from auggie token print run as the creating user via AUGMENT_SESSION_AUTH; --show-cost prints cost per print-mode run.

evidence.title: Service Accounts
evidence.locator: About; Managing; Creating API tokens; Deleting
evidence.finding: Team and Enterprise tenant admins create service accounts with non-expiring API tokens (session.json); deleting a token or account is permanent and disrupts automations using it.

evidence.title: Context Engine MCP
evidence.locator: Local vs Remote Server; Usage cost; How Indexing Works; Connect to MCP
evidence.finding: Context Engine is exposed over MCP locally (Auggie as stdio server, real-time working-directory index) or remotely over HTTP (selected repos' default branches via GitHub App), with OAuth or API key auth; it offers codebase-retrieval to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Zed and others. Queries bill at token pricing plus the 40% fee.

evidence.title: Auggie SDK
evidence.finding: TypeScript (@augmentcode/auggie-sdk) and Python (auggie-sdk) SDKs with session-file, env-var or apiKey auth and custom tools.

evidence.title: Self-Hosted Daemon Pools
evidence.finding: Pools route sessions to an eligible daemon by workspace requirements and current load; isolated (git worktree) or shared workspace modes; pool bundles are a Preview CLI feature.

evidence.title: Configuring Triggers
evidence.locator: Trigger Types; Adding a Trigger; Event Type Reference; Payload Filters
evidence.finding: Triggers open a session with the event payload: first-party GitHub, Linear, Slack, GitLab and PagerDuty (Cosmos owns upstream registration), cron schedules, and custom HTTPS webhooks. JSONLogic filters, optional max runs per minute, and Run sessions as the creator or a service account.

evidence.title: Plugins and Marketplaces
evidence.finding: Plugins bundle custom commands, subagents, hooks, skills and MCP servers, distributed through Git-repository marketplaces and enabled per user, project or local settings file.

evidence.title: Rules
evidence.locator: Rule locations; User vs Workspace; Frontmatter
evidence.finding: Loads workspace .augment/rules, user ~/.augment/rules, AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) from the current and parent directories and .augment-guidelines; user rules always apply, workspace rules support always_apply, agent_requested and manual.

evidence.title: Skills
evidence.finding: Skills load from .augment/skills, .claude/skills or .agents/skills in the workspace or home directory.

evidence.title: Tool Permissions
evidence.locator: Intro; Permission Types and Precedence; Settings files; Allow/Block lists
evidence.finding: toolPermissions rules (allow, deny, ask-user, webhook-policy, script-policy) are honored by Auggie CLI and Cosmos cloud agents but not the IDE extension; most restrictive wins; ask-user denies without a UI; managed settings at /etc/augment/settings.json; shell rules match by regex; unmatched tools follow implicit runtime behavior; a committed .augment/settings.json enforces policy on cloud agents.

evidence.title: Subagents
evidence.locator: Overview; Configuration fields; Tool restrictions; Supported models
evidence.finding: Subagents run in parallel; built-in general-purpose, explore and plan agents; custom agents set model, thinking level and a tools allowlist or disabled_tools; codebase-retrieval searches the codebase.

evidence.title: Ticket Dispatcher
evidence.finding: Runs on a schedule, scans configured ticket sources, applies a readiness rubric, dispatches PR Author for ready tickets, respects a maximum of dispatcher-owned open changes and records skip reasons.

evidence.title: Feedback Triager
evidence.locator: Feedback Triager; Tickets and next steps
evidence.finding: Each new top-level Slack message starts a session that claims the thread, classifies and investigates; it creates tickets in Linear, Jira or GitHub Issues automatically or on request after searching for duplicates, and never changes code itself.

evidence.title: Using Schedules as Triggers
evidence.locator: Adding a Schedule; Concurrency and Reliability
evidence.finding: 5-field cron with IANA timezone. Each schedule runs in singleton mode: a fire that arrives while the previous run executes is skipped, not queued. Missed fires during pod transitions or leadership changes are not backfilled. Sessions run with the creator's permissions.

evidence.title: Manage automations
evidence.locator: Overview; Run History; Event History; Inspect events across automations
evidence.finding: Automation pages show triggers with pause toggles, Run History with succeeded/failed counts for 24 hours and 7 days and each run's session (with its worker tree in the sidebar), Event History, and a cross-automation Event Log with payloads and headers.

evidence.title: Managing Spaces
evidence.finding: Sessions, Experts, environments, secrets and MCP servers belong to Spaces; a worker launched by a manager inherits the manager's Space so the worker subtree stays together. Any member can create a Space and becomes its owner; renaming, deleting and membership changes need an org admin or owner.

evidence.title: Cosmos Experts
evidence.locator: Overview; Sharing; What an Expert includes
evidence.finding: Experts package system prompt, instructions, integrations, environment, model and worker Experts; shared privately, with teammates, a Space or the organization; Advisor can configure them.

evidence.title: Expert templates
evidence.finding: Templates include Cosmos Advisor, PR Author, PR Fixer, Risk Analyzer, Deep Reviewer, Pair Reviewer, Verifier, Incident Investigator, Feedback Triager, Project Builder, Ticket Manager, Ticket Dispatcher, Data Analyst, ROI Analyst and Code Review Memory.

evidence.title: What's new in Auggie 1.x
evidence.finding: Auggie 1.x prerelease adds /export to HTML or JSONL and /import to resume from JSONL, compaction, worktrees, a permissions manager and Notification hooks.

evidence.title: CLI Reference
evidence.finding: auggie --continue resumes the most recent session, --resume picks a saved session, --export converts a session JSONL to HTML.

evidence.title: Migrate Code Review to Cosmos
evidence.finding: The current Code Review bot on GitHub will be sunset; a guide moves reviews to Cosmos Deep Reviewer.

evidence.title: Project Builder
evidence.finding: Takes a large feature through design, architecture and ticket breakdown, then launches a PR Author worker per unit in dependency waves; never merges.

evidence.title: Understanding Files
evidence.locator: Scopes; Browsing; Versioning and Recovery; Limits
evidence.finding: Files persist across sessions in User or Organization scope, sync at turn boundaries, show the agent that last wrote each file, and keep immutable attributed versions with time-decayed pruning; 1 MB per file, 100 MB per filesystem.

evidence.title: Understanding Artifacts
evidence.locator: About; Artifact types; Searching; Adding manually
evidence.finding: Sessions store PR, Git branch, Linear issue (feature-flagged) and custom link artifacts; PRs opened through the GitHub tool attach automatically; Cmd+K finds sessions by PR, branch or Linear ID. Artifacts are per session.

evidence.title: PR Fixer
evidence.finding: Repairs review findings, CI failures and unambiguous merge conflicts on changes created without PR Author; never merges.

evidence.title: Configure a code review pipeline
evidence.finding: Risk Analyzer classifies each change and auto-approves intrinsically low-risk changes per org policy while routing higher-risk ones; Deep Reviewer reviews line by line; Pair Reviewer posts comments; cosmos approve evaluates a current-head approval policy (disabled by default) requiring no unresolved findings or comments.

evidence.title: Okta Express Configuration
evidence.finding: Okta JIT provisioning creates users on first login; Universal Logout lets Okta terminate sessions and tokens.

evidence.title: Index your workspace
evidence.finding: Opening a workspace uploads the codebase to Augment's cloud for indexing; .gitignore and .augmentignore control what is indexed.

evidence.title: Daemon Configuration File
evidence.finding: maxAgents caps concurrent child-agent sessions per daemon (default 100); allowIndexing defaults to false.

evidence.title: Hooks
evidence.finding: Hook timeout defaults to 60000 ms.

evidence.title: Secrets Manager
evidence.finding: Secrets are encrypted, write-only, stripped from logs and exported into the VM at boot only when the session is authorized, the secret applies to its Space and auto-install is on.

evidence.title: augmentcode/auggie repository
evidence.finding: The public repo at 8bd7186 holds docs, examples, a plugin marketplace, slash-command files and workflows under a custom proprietary license; the CLI and Cosmos source are not included.

evidence.title: Auggie releases
evidence.finding: v1.2.2 on 2026-11-17 and v1.3.0 prerelease builds several times a day from 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-20.

evidence.title: What's new in Auggie 1.x
evidence.finding: Auggie 1.x exports sessions as HTML or JSONL and resumes JSONL via /import; the page still labels 1.x prerelease.

evidence.title: Managing Cosmos with auggie cloud
evidence.finding: Experts, environments, MCP servers and residents use YAML bundles; export writes a remote resource locally and apply creates or updates it with an immutable version.

evidence.title: Configure a code review pipeline
evidence.locator: Deep Reviewer; Verifier; PR Dashboard Manager; cosmos approve
evidence.finding: Per-PR Dashboard Manager summarizes Expert status, evidence, reviewed commits and actions. PR Fixer can repair Deep Reviewer findings. Disabled-by-default cosmos approve can require current-head review and no unaddressed Verifier defect against the current commit; approval never merges.

evidence.title: Ticket Dispatcher
evidence.finding: Ticket Dispatcher exposes backpressure limits and caps dispatcher-owned open changes to avoid flooding the review queue.

evidence.title: Using Sessions
evidence.finding: Shared sessions are readable by the organization; the owner may grant individual teammates viewer access. Conversation persists, but an environment paused for a long time may restart clean and lose uncommitted changes.

evidence.title: Feedback Triager
evidence.finding: Feedback Triager searches the configured tracker for plausible duplicates before filing; repeated requests reuse the existing result rather than repeating side effects.
